summary: This release uses stock OMP v18.12.5 as its engineering baseline. The 56 changelog entries below record the changes since v0.8.0. Historical receipts do not qualify these bytes.
highlights:
- This release uses stock OMP v18.12.5 as its engineering baseline. The 56 changelog entries below record the changes since v0.8.0. Historical receipts do not qualify these bytes.
- Qualification-only private rotating structured gateway logs and bounded Push send/ack evidence. Push recovery permits one evidence-backed fresh ask per phase, preserves existing delivery bounds, records late posts and per-delivery timings, and stops unexplained timeouts without retry. Durable write-ahead log health, retained-host raw-stream proof, explicit runtime protocol negotiation, outbound-clear acknowledgement, and drained cancellation preserve recovery evidence across failure. Synchronous log bursts coalesce durability barriers; retained-Mac proof paths remain POSIX on every host. Recovery binds opaque qualification aliases to the exact fixture ask before mutation. Bracketed log reads, committed rotation boundaries, durable local retention and sticky search-permission failures preserve evidence; bounded nested Android operations retain late-created targets and readiness late posts. An in-directory writer lease rejects unclosed histories even when failure writes are impossible. Unproven CDP target/forward cleanup blocks Pixel release; task restoration cannot reopen CDP. Re-arm rechecks generation before mutation, metadata timeouts retain late sampling, and post-evidence deadline checks plus bounded integer phase durations prevent stale delivery success. Writer/collector exclusion and atomic log-directory retirement close retention races; forced HTTP shutdown drains admitted handlers before releasing the durable writer claim. Readiness checks both delivery and clear budgets after awaited evidence, every persisted duration is a bounded integer, and network fallbacks preserve containment failures. Cleanup checks source-scoped v2 triage stores; guarded fixture asks reject a changed acknowledged session at the extension boundary. Portable fixture regressions prove Windows permission refusal without relaxing POSIX admission; bounded CLI startup failures retain fixed diagnostic booleans without extending the two-second exit assertion. Readiness failure timing starts before mutation and evidence-construction failure cannot skip restoration. Request attestation preserves containment on expiry; snapshot faults retain their identity, clear budgets include metadata work, and late samplers follow ask settlement and delivery.
- Automatic same-candidate qualification retries for validated, fully contained infrastructure failures: attempts 0–2, persisted 60/120-second backoff, immutable failed-attempt evidence, exact-owner lease retention and privacy-safe tracking comments. Product, harness, unknown, mixed, dirty and exhausted failures stop; historical device-cloud holds remain manual. Retry authority requires agreeing observed terminal evidence and original outcome/log digests; pending plans retain failed-job identity until launch, and probe the live OS lock without changing ownership. Receiptless retries require an explicit effect-free predecessor proof. All retries consume predecessor authority before renewed admission; standalone preflight is restricted to the initial attempt.
- Closed qualification failure and machine-outcome contracts, POSIX-only private atomic outcome persistence, and additive schema-3 receipt validation, including paired private readiness owner epochs and closed phases. Complete owner-bound failure graphs, effects-free preflight boundaries and containment-consistent outcomes fail closed; resumed attempts clear stale failure authority. Unknown, mixed, unresolved or unbound failures remain non-retryable; this change does not enable automatic recovery or reinterpret historical failures.
- Finalize failed stable campaigns after healthy siblings settle, complete independent OMP publication lifecycle proof, and retain typed collateral evidence for an unrestored Pixel. Add an effectful rig-readiness gate with device/service restoration before expensive fan-out, bounded owner cancellation, and exact-bound failed-attempt recovery without rewriting passed proofs. Fence fresh retry ordinals, validate every persisted receipt, preserve admission failure ownership, restore poisoned resources despite checkpoint failures, and reap remote fixture process groups before cleanup. Readiness and provider cancellation retain one failure allocator and terminal proof. Fence every retained-Mac command path after unproved termination, retain command owners through settlement, preserve passed publication proofs on relay teardown failure, validate execution and artifact bindings before writes, and restore every readiness owner despite persistence failures. Keep cleanup/reconciliation/persistence failures monotonic across later successful cleanup; preserve failure identities and Pixel poisoning through terminal writes. Unify shell uploads, PTYs and reboot ownership behind whole-process-group settlement, retain fixtures for unresolved cloud/Push owners, and propagate Windows physical-client/restoration cancellation. Readiness explicitly does not yet restore byte-identical private installation state.
- Structured Windows transport failure evidence, bounded read-only reconnects, deadline-aware subprocess reaping, and interrupted-upload reconciliation without write replay. Cleanup skips confirmed-absent guests and treats guest-command failures as diagnostic only after VM destruction, while retaining independent firewall, tailnet, Pixel, and vault containment requirements. Commit containment before deleting recovery state; fence incomplete same-epoch uploads, unknown process exits, legacy staging without upload claims, and cancellation races instead of recovering them as successful work. Retire the old epoch vault before replacing development identity, and require settled provider inventory before cleanup completion. Fence every guest mutation with durable single-shot claims, preserve committed containment during retirement failures, and share one allocation/admission deadline from before firewall creation. Refuse cancelled final evidence and contradictory transport status; keep POSIX signal-escalation coverage off Windows runners. Check allocation expiry immediately before creation POSTs, settle firewall-only recovery vaults without false ownership vetoes, contain cancelled development attempts, and reject late poll success. FreeRDP input failures reap their child; resumed admission retains stability evidence. Retained-state refusals and preflight failures enter independent containment; expired local budgets carry typed controller-deadline evidence. Completed admission resumes under reconnect bounds, and expired creation authority cannot consume the private creation counter.
- Retain redacted qualification cause chains and stacks on private CLI stderr, plus an exclusive private readiness browser-substep diagnostic with the CDP method, without changing receipts. Preserve causes across lane ownership and deadlines, bound private bytes, and keep diagnostic retention failures outside the sanitized failure graph. Preserve ordinary caught errors and aggregate readiness metrics, redact nested opt-out markers before emission, and propagate whole-chain diagnostic flags without duplicating abort roots.
- Accept fully acknowledged Push fan-out for one request alias, retain bounded recipient/send/ack counts, and refuse stale retained-rig subscriptions before the readiness ask. Attribute browser baseline failures to closed browser/CDP substeps while preserving restoration and operator-only subscription recovery. Bind readiness counters to the final snapshot, require lock-screen presentation and clear proofs, reject out-of-order telemetry, and preserve execution deadlines.
- Retain bounded, byte-exact qualification child stdout/stderr in immutable private release-driver job logs for successful and failed campaigns, retries and preflights before terminal publication. Bind both logs into the retry plan's job digest without changing sanitized diagnostics or public announcements.
- Re-enter only the current process's retained development Pixel lease during automatic cleanup, bounded by its fresh cleanup deadline; preserve foreign or changed ownership. Attribute execution-clipped helper timers to controller expiry, recheck rejected mutations, and guard the resource lifetime at final guest dispatch. Parse complete Windows fetch options and the same dispatcher's GET-only gate; reject overriding options and legacy unguarded callbacks.
- Retain an initial Windows development guest only for a typed, known-disposition product assertion; contain infrastructure, authentication, harness, unknown, and expired attempts. Guard firewall-rule POSTs after refetch, helper spawns after checkpoints, and every owned effect boundary; reject late successful or failed observations with one positive-budget guard instead of launching 1-ms probes. Arm subprocess cancellation before work and switch provider/guest/Pixel dispatch to the cleanup owner. Admit only reviewed guarded Windows fetch forms in repository policy while preserving GET-only retries.
- Contain browser CI flakes with one CI-only retry across both mobile Chromium and cross-engine core suites, closed privacy-safe attempt reports and summaries retained for 14 days, and a weekly/manual seven-day flake budget with fail-closed evidence coverage. Local runs keep zero retries and prepare PRs still execute their own required checks. Reject response-completion, request-finished and network-idle readiness waits in e2e; the delayed-resume tray race now waits for an applied local row transition while its remote snapshot remains held.
- Derive browser flake outcomes from attempt/expected-status evidence, bind HTTP-assertion lint exemptions to the same lexical response, and assess coverage from actually executed browser jobs so cancellation/selective reruns do not invent missing evidence. Validate explicitly pinned fleet targets separately from workflow heads; version-2 cohorts exclude pre-contract reports. The delayed-resume regression also waits for remote generation reconciliation before asserting that the mounted foreground shell was not superseded.
- Opt-in **New session** creation in Tern from administrator-approved project, working-copy, and profile choices on the execution host, with durable identity-scoped idempotency, lossless local block/pane and basename correlation, OMP-native adoption into **Control**, conservative interrupted/unknown outcome handling, and automatic `tern` removal on rollback with `<configDir>/config.pre-rollback.json` backup ([ADR-043](docs/DECISIONS.md#adr-043--opt-in-tern-creation-with-omp-native-adoption)). The PWA's **Create and open Control** wizard shows progress as three steps, replays a lost-acknowledgement request only within one hour, and never recreates on an uncertain outcome. Embedded sessions report snapshot progress (`Joining session… 43%` / `Reconnecting… 43%`) in the connection status chip and accept an optional memory-only **First task** draft once into an empty writable Control composer without auto-sending; native **Open in Tern** handoff remains upstream-blocked on Android ([tern-sdk #143](https://github.com/stencil-hq/tern-sdk/issues/143)) and deferred on desktop.
- Resumable, skippable first-run trays for connection facts, optional background alerts, and View versus Control, reusing the existing tray and notification control. The bounded `omp.sessions.first-run.v1` record stores only step and timestamp. A same-scope queue clearance gets one emerald all-clear arrival, mirrored by the shell's answered check draw-in; fresh loads, routine refreshes, scope changes and reduced motion remain still (ADR-042).
- Unify Settings, Troubleshooting, Hide/Undo and request Options in one native tray system. Open request connects inside an amber tray and expands into the same live session without replacing its client, socket or composer draft. Nested focus/back, grip dismissal, safe areas, paused Undo expiry and reduced-motion paths share one implementation (ADR-041). Requests use one session-identity header and a flat client frame; Undo is a compact tile/copy/action notice, and the hero's quiet Options chip is visibly tappable. Keep successive requests coordinated with expansion and cancellation, let foreground choices supersede background resume, and return keyboard focus to the request after closing its tray.
- Document same-uid/private-ACL discovery for isolated OMP HOMEs and the unchanged 18.12.5→18.12.6 collaboration contract; extend the local lifecycle proof with native-executable publication, real View/Control attach, restart and OMP-owned revocation checks, without changing the engineering baseline lock.
- Give every session the identity Tern shows for it: a light tile holding the title's leading Nerd Font icon (or a monogram) with the session state as a corner badge, two-line titles, and a metadata line of whole facts (project · state · uptime with day units · model) that wraps between facts instead of truncating each one; hosts appear only while several are in view, the host picker becomes one compact scope control, `Hide` becomes an icon-only control with the same accessible name, and incomplete host coverage shows an amber dot.
- Move between the directory and a session with a shared-axis slide in which the tapped tile becomes the session header's tile, and move rows when a session changes group, is hidden, or returns, with the heading cross-fading between `Sessions` and `Needs you` — Material emphasized curves, 200–400 ms, typed same-document view transitions gated on a structural signature so a routine refresh never animates; `prefers-reduced-motion` and unsupported browsers render the same DOM without motion; a row keeps its tile and facts while its session opens (ADR-040).
- Show one connection-interruption story in the directory banner, reserve host rows for independently failed sources, and keep routine refreshes quiet with no Retry action.
- Report host coverage as counts without repeating host names; mark cached sessions and their counts as listed rather than live, using one consistent “list as of” clock.
- Keep empty and host-filtered directories informative when coverage is incomplete, without claiming there are no sessions on an unreachable or unauthorized host.
- Remove Retry from access-denied hosts; restoring access requires an operator or identity change.
- Keep session outage names in the connection chip and recovery timing in the triage bar, without repeating the same warning.
- Show initial session joins as neutral progress until gateway/relay health reports a fault; keep the fault name visible in compact request trays as well as full sessions.
- Replace unavailable Create actions with recovery choices, distinguish uncertain creation from failure, and identify Create-and-Control as a privileged action.
- Refresh the embedded OMP client and wire pin to v18.12.6: coalesce streaming renders and parse only Markdown tails (#14728), take linear-time Markdown/math lexing (#13961, #14667), stop idle agent-drawer polling, and adopt the eval renderer rework. Vendor the pure-JavaScript marked fork without native dependencies; retain gateway capability, Ask/photo/speech, recovery, artwork, and Show earlier behavior, including coalescing-safe return-to-tail. Transcript PUA symbols use the gateway's self-hosted Nerd Font fallback; the host baseline remains v18.12.5.
- Keep failed local targets distinct from an open remote session, including Next, Hold, and withdrawn Control actions.
- Clear expired-target notices after successful list recovery instead of recreating a resolved failure.
- Restore Hold immediately when a target failure is dismissed while its list refresh is still pending.
- Build a newly opened session's title and Control action from the latest authoritative metadata.
- Show a shared empty-list clock only when the hosts' observation instants actually match.
- Preserve cross-host Next and Hold failure notices through updates from the session still on screen, until dismissal or target recovery.
- Mark target-host access denial in red, distinct from amber connection or launch failures.
- Reject an in-flight session launch when View or Control is withdrawn, including launches resumed after browser restoration.
- Keep a newer session choice authoritative even when its launch fails while an older browser restoration is waiting.
- Resume pending request previews after a browser back/forward-cache restore without reusing an old launch.
- Restore remote sessions and update their request triage even when local authorization or the local list is unavailable.
- Attribute failed cross-host Next-ask actions to the target host and refresh expired target lists without replaying a launch.
- Return failed or changed request previews to the directory without retaining an obsolete host-selection snapshot.
- Show independently confirmed remote empty lists and retain empty-observation clocks during quiet rechecks.
- Preserve local connection faults and recovery across phone backgrounding and remote-session opens.
- Withdraw local sessions and invalidate old live events after authorization denial from launch, creation, or embedded probes, not only directory-list requests.
- Keep remote expired-session and failed-launch feedback on that host instead of replacing a local fault.
- Explain withdrawn, expired, and retained-empty observations in All hosts and single-host directories.
- Restore the current directory scope after a request preview is denied or cancelled.
- Keep the named connection fault visible while retrying a failed first session list.
- Report a remote launch access denial on that host alone, preserving the local connection story.
- Keep accepted session creation attached to the same host when fleet configuration recovers.
- Distinguish an authorization-withdrawn list from an observed empty list, even after going offline.
- Keep remote observations stale and bounded while offline, and resume polling after scheduled recovery even when the browser never emits an online event.
- Give failed fleet bootstrap one banner owner and retry it when the local connection recovers.
- Preserve the last successful empty-list clock, accessible Listed vocabulary, and neutral checking copy in held queues and answer feedback.
- Render Nerd Font Private Use Area symbols in session titles with a self-hosted Symbols Nerd Font Mono subset, split into immutable, content-hashed WOFF2 chunks loaded and cached only on first use; keep ordinary text on system fonts and make no remote font requests.
- Refuse a missing Pixel Tailscale/DNS path to the configured gateway before Android acceptance navigation, with named reachability/adb diagnostics and a read-only parent admission gate that does not poison the shared Pixel lease before a mutating child has run (#430).
- Recount prepared changelog entry-count drift against `release-text.json` before qualification, preserving every bullet, the exact requested candidate and immutable release records (#436).
- Keep local 21-case visual validation required while making only Percy upload failures advisory, with visible local/upload outcomes and capability-free diagnostic artifacts. Snapshot queueing no longer claims confirmed submission before build finalization.

stableRollback: The selected predecessor is v0.8.0. Gateway rollback does not switch or restart the separately running OMP process. This release uses stock OMP v18.12.5. rollback --to selects only retained runtimes. Preserve configuration and readiness-token state; see docs/UPGRADE_ROLLBACK.md for predecessor compatibility and stopped-service recovery.
